thread:
alex: Pushed a Grafana panel for prefix/prompt cache observability — per-model + per-route + per-customer hit_rate and tokens_saved. Sharing TL;DR and asking for design/alert thoughts.

maya: Nice! can you paste the metric names? also curious how tokens_saved is computed.

alex: metric names are: `prefix_cache.hits`, `prefix_cache.requests`, `prefix_cache.tokens_saved`. hit_rate = hits / requests. tokens_saved is sum of matched_prefix_token_count across requests (we store matched_token_count in the cache event).

sam: Are we keying cache by (model, route, customer, normalized_prompt_prefix)? last perf run showed poor global hit_rate because keying included small non-deterministic headers.

alex: Keying currently: model_id + route_id + customer_id + canonicalized_prefix. Canonicalization strips ephemeral tokens and normalizes whitespace. We still get fragmentation for templated prompts with per-user ids. Thinking of adding a per-route prefix-scrub rule.

olivia: For dashboards, would like a stacked breakdown: served tokens vs saved tokens per model, with a derived metric 'pct_tokens_saved = tokens_saved / total_tokens_generated'. Also add 95th p95 reduction in token time cost if possible.

jordan: Two quick asks: 1) add a time-to-warmup curve per model (percent hit_rate over first 10k requests) so we can see warmup bias. 2) an anomaly rule when tokens_saved per-minute drops >50% vs rolling-24h baseline.

alex: Good calls. I added a warmup panel using a histogram aggregation by bucketed request_count windows. Query snippet in PromQL-esque pseudo: 
```
sum by(model_id, route_id)(increase(prefix_cache.tokens_saved[1h]))
/ sum by(model_id, route_id)(increase(prefix_cache.tokens_generated[1h]))
```
This feeds the tokens_saved rate. Warmup curve: compute hit_rate over sliding cumulative windows (0..10k).

maya: Could we surface per-customer top-10 prefixes by token-saved? That would help SRE / customer success to see wins. Maybe a table with top prefix hashes and examples.

alex: Yep, added an internal-only table panel that lists prefix_hash, example_snippet (truncated), hit_rate, tokens_saved, sample_rate. sample_rate > 0.1 by default for low-frequency customers to avoid cold-start noise.

sam: Perf regression note: in last canary we saw a drop in hit_rate for `gpt-open-legacy` model from 38% -> 21%. Root cause was a change in kernel packing that altered sequence padding behavior and bumped canonicalization hash. Reverted the packing change and hit_rate recovered. We should add an integration test that compares cache key stability across kernel variants.

olivia: Agree. Add a CI job that runs a deterministic prefix set through each kernel selection path and asserts identical canonicalized_prefix output. Place results in artifacts and fail CI on mismatch.

infra-bot: Deploy finished: grafana/dashboard/prefix-cache-observability updated (rev 3). Panels: per-model hit_rate, per-route tokens_saved, per-customer top-prefixes, warmup-curves.

jordan: For alerts, propose two: (A) tokens_saved per-minute drop >50% vs 24h baseline for any model OR customer (severity P2). (B) total_hit_rate < 10% for any production route for >15m (severity P1). Thoughts?

maya: Sounds good. For B, also trigger an automated rollback to previous canonicalization config if the CI key-stability test fails after a deploy.

alex: I'll wire the alerts and add a runbook stub in /runbooks/cache-issues.md with quick triage steps: check key hash diffs, recent kernel/runtime changes, recent deploys by commit.

sam: One last note: we should expose sample-weighted hit_rate (so very large requests don't dominate). Use tokens_generated as weight.

alex: Done. Updated panel to show both raw hit_rate and token-weighted hit_rate. Will watch dashboards tomorrow morning and post a short summary. :eyes:

olivia: Thanks — will loop in CS for early access to per-customer panel.

alex: Thanks all. If anyone wants edit access to the grafana folder ping me.
